office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering the tax structure, school and child-care funding, housing and landlord-tenant law, behavioral-health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: A 2024 rematch in central Spokane: Democratic incumbent Natasha Hill, who took 64.5% in the August primary, faces Republican Tony Kiepe. Hill campaigns on the 2026 millionaires tax and housing legislation; Kiepe runs on a full state budget audit, no new taxes and more police and jail capacity.

candidates.summary: One-term Democratic incumbent, Vice Chair of the House Housing Committee and civil litigation attorney from Hillyard, whose record includes votes for the 2026 millionaires tax and the 2025 rent-increase limits.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and says she "led on" it [S1][S3]
Voted for the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases (EHB 1217) and has called for rent stabilization [S5][S9]
Voted for ESHB 1296 and is listed as opposing I-001 and I-638 [S4][S10]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346; independently says she led on the millionaire tax, platform calls for the wealthy to pay an equitable share, and backed keeping the capital gains tax.

spending.basis: Co-wrote an op-ed urging rejection of child-care and early-learning cuts; platform supports investment in treatment, housing and job training.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent-increase limits and called for statewide rent stabilization, while also backing supply measures such as condominium reform and land banks.

safety.basis: Says incarceration without care is not effective and supports investment in mental health, addiction treatment, housing and job training.

climate.basis: Platform supports a just transition away from fossil fuels and clean-energy investment; no specific carbon-pricing record in the dossier.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2025 with two sessions and a committee vice chair post; shorter tenure than a long-serving legislator, against a never-elected opponent.

immigration.basis: Says she supported critical protections for immigrants; co-wrote an op-ed criticizing federal prosecution of ICE-facility protesters.

social.basis: Platform pledges to champion safe access to abortion; publicly listed as opposing I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights law, and is listed as opposing I-001, which would restore it.

candidates.summary: Republican Medicare insurance agent and chair of the Spokane County Conservancy Board, running a second time for the seat on a full state budget audit, fiscal restraint and law enforcement.
highlights: Priorities: "full budget audit," affordable housing, thriving businesses and fiscal responsibility [S2]
Says "the answer is not tax more" and the state should make cuts instead of raising taxes [S3]
Wants more police, "keeping criminals in jail" and investment in a jail [S3]

taxes.basis: Questionnaire rejects raising taxes in favor of cuts; a single source without a specific tax pledge or plan.

spending.basis: Website and questionnaire both center a complete government audit, cutting waste and defunding programs that do not show results.

housing.basis: Attributes high building costs to bureaucracy and permitting fees and supports faster permitting; no tenant-protection or public-housing proposals.

safety.basis: Calls funding police the first priority, wants to keep criminals in jail and build jail capacity; named enforcement as the top issue in 2024 as well.

experience.basis: No elected experience; several unsuccessful city council and House bids.
